name: roofs_mixed_d
prompt:
Two images are attached. The first is a layout: 8 building outlines seen from above, in a 3×3 grid on a flat magenta background. The second is finished art from the same game, to match in style only — not its layout, shapes, colours or the size of its details.

Make one image with exactly the same 3×3 layout as the first image. Inside each outline, draw the roof of the building described for that cell below, as a top-down sprite for a 2D city game.

Shape comes first. Before painting a cell, trace its outline exactly, then paint only inside the traced border:
- Keep every outline's proportions: match each one's width and height. Each cell's proportion is given below; check it. Never make an outline squarer, shorter or fatter.
- Every edge is straight and square to the others. Never slant, skew or taper an edge to show perspective. An outline built of several rectangles (an L, a T, a stepped block) is followed corner by corner.
- Draw nothing outside the outline: no eaves, steps, porches, canopies, ramps or shadows past it. A porch or an entrance canopy is drawn inside the outline at its bottom edge. Inside a roof there is no magenta at all.

Scale is the second rule, and it is strict. Every size below is true metres, width × depth, and every detail is drawn at its true size against them. These buildings stand beside cars 4 m long and 1.8 m wide; keep that in mind for every detail. True sizes:
- hospital: a plant room about 3 × 4 m; an air conditioner unit about 1–1.5 m; a parapet about 0.4 m thick.
- garages: each lock-up is about 3 m wide with a 2.5 m door on the street edge; a parapet between units about 0.3 m.
- retail: an air conditioner unit about 1 × 1 m; a vent about 0.5 m; a plain sign strip about 0.6 m deep along the front; a parapet about 0.3 m thick.
- tower: a lift machine room about 3 × 5 m; a hatch or vent shaft about 1 m; a TV antenna about 2 m across; a parapet about 0.4 m thick; drain funnels about 0.4 m.
- school: an air conditioner unit about 1 m; a skylight about 1.5 m; a parapet about 0.4 m thick; tile courses about 0.25 m apart on pitched wings.
- office: a plant room about 3 × 4 m; an air conditioner unit about 1–1.5 m; a chiller about 2 × 4 m; a parapet about 0.4 m thick; a roof hatch about 1 m.
- No detail is bigger than its true size. When in doubt, draw it smaller and keep fewer of them. A large roof has many small details, never a few huge ones.

Rules for every cell:
- Look straight down (orthographic). No perspective, no walls seen from the side, no tilt, no ground, no plants, no cars, no people.
- The thick bottom edge of each outline is the street front, where the entrance is. The top edge is the back.
- A gabled roof shows its ridge as one line with the two slopes shaded differently; a lean-to roof is one slope with no ridge; a flat roof has a parapet round its edge.
- Style: match the style image. Clean, flat-shaded cartoon game art, bold dark outlines, muted natural colours, simple readable details, soft light from the top-left.
- Outside the roofs, keep the background flat pure magenta #FF00FF. No text, letters, numbers, labels, logos, grid lines or frames anywhere.

Cells, left to right, top to bottom:

Row 1
1. 16.8 × 8.4 m (2.0× wider than deep) — hospital or clinic wing, flat grey roof with rooftop plant, ducts and a lift room
2. 15 × 11.1 m (1.4× wider than deep) — row of 4 lock-up garages of a garage cooperative, flat roof of rusty corrugated metal parted by low brick parapets between the units, patched in places
3. 7.8 × 11.1 m (1.4× deeper than wide) — single-storey shop pavilion, flat grey roof with an air conditioner unit and a sign along the front edge, standing narrow end to the street with the entrance on that short front wall

Row 2
4. 15.6 × 11.1 m (1.4× wider than deep) — single-storey shop pavilion, flat grey roof with an air conditioner unit and a sign along the front edge
5. 8.5 × 11.1 m (1.3× deeper than wide) — stair and lift core of a tall block, flat grey roof filled by the lift machine room and a roof exit, standing narrow end to the street with the entrance on that short front wall
6. 5.6 × 11.2 m (2.0× deeper than wide) — small single-storey annex of a clinic, flat grey roof with a vent and an air conditioner unit, standing narrow end to the street with the entrance on that short front wall

Row 3
7. 16.8 × 11.2 m (1.5× wider than deep) — Soviet-era school or college wing, flat bitumen roof with a parapet, roof exits and ventilation stacks
8. 7.5 × 11.5 m (1.5× deeper than wide) — mid-rise office or public building, flat roof of light gravel ballast with rooftop plant, a lift room and a parapet, standing narrow end to the street with the entrance on that short front wall
